argument: Increasing the angular dispersion of arriving particles toward more horizontal trajectories enhances the shadowing effect, leading to faster column growth, larger separation between columns, and wider dispersion of column heights in thin-film growth by PECVD.
boundary: Evidence is limited to the reported KMC simulations of TiO2 and ZnO thin films under the specified growth conditions; transfer to other materials or deposition methods is unestablished.
claim: Increasing the angular dispersion of arriving particles toward more horizontal trajectories enhances the shadowing effect, leading to faster column growth, larger separation between columns, and wider dispersion of column heights in thin-film growth by PECVD.
